policy.LEAF-1: A foldout may leave the room for three evenings. Start counting on the evening it leaves.
policy.LEAF-2: On a credit slip for a joint print, put the studio name first, a colon next, and the print title last.
policy.LEAF-3: This edition approves only dry linen wraps. For any unlisted finish, withhold permission and refer the request to the pattern desk.
policy.LEAF-4: A shelf placard may separate its aisle name and color with either a slash or a vertical bar. Neither divider has priority.

cases.prompt: How many evenings can I borrow a foldout, and when do I start counting? Cite the room rule.

baseline.text: Three evenings. The evening you take it out is evening one. [LEAF-1]

candidate.text: Count the evening it leaves as the first of your three evenings [LEAF-1].

demo_vote.reason: Both give the same duration and the same counting rule, with the right citation.

cases.prompt: I have a new pleated paper finish. May I use it to wrap a print today? Cite your authority or tell me who can decide.

baseline.text: Yes. Paper is dry, so it qualifies under the dry-wrap rule [LEAF-3].

candidate.text: I can't approve pleated paper under this edition. Only dry linen is listed; ask the pattern desk before using another finish [LEAF-3].

demo_vote.reason: Dry paper is not dry linen. Withholding permission and naming the desk avoids an unsupported approval.

cases.prompt: Studio Thimble Row made the joint print Low Tide. What should I write on its credit slip? Include the clause.

baseline.text: Start with the studio, add a colon, then write the print title [LEAF-2].

candidate.text: Write “Thimble Row: Low Tide” on the slip [LEAF-2].

demo_vote.reason: Both give the prescribed format, but only one supplies a line the requester can copy.

cases.prompt: Write a Python function tabs(labels) returning the nonblank labels after trimming edge whitespace. Keep input order and repeated labels. The cards contain synthetic, pre-recorded observations, not a live test run.

demo_vote.reason: The repeat example loses the second ink tab in one response; repeats were explicitly required.

cases.prompt: Mock up one allowed placard for aisle Ridge and color Silt. Tell me if the rule specifies which divider will read better from the far shelf.

baseline.text: Ridge / Silt. The room permits both dividers and says nothing about distance readability [LEAF-4].

candidate.text: Ridge | Silt. Neither mark is preferred by the rule [LEAF-4]; try a sample at shelf distance.

demo_vote.reason: Both are allowed. No placard at the actual viewing distance is provided to judge legibility.
